# fix: ai-fill-hour (2DD9:0DD9 ai_fill_program_slot, instruction 2DD9:1289 mov al,[bp-17h])
# The audience estimate 32BA:03BC gets the programme category as its hour.  New game, the human
# only presses Esc.  Test pokes: computer player 2's minimum viewers (g_ai_ad_req[2] +2, u32 at
# 39D4:7772/7774) held at 600000 every 100 frames (the game recomputes it from its contracts).
# Day 1, ~19:00, player 2 fills hour slot 5 (22:00) from films 88 (love, 3 hours), 104 (X-rated
# action), 129 (action) and 198 (comedy).  Classic: 129 is estimated for "hour" 2 (19:00) =
# 487872 viewers < 600000, 104 for 19:00 = 0 (X-rated films count 0 before 21:00), and 88's
# estimate for "hour" 1 (18:00) keeps it out too -> 198 ("hour" 4) passes -> slot 5 = 198
# (88 later goes to slot 9).  Fixed: all estimated for 22:00 (104: 1047200, 129: 1256640,
# 198: 1116192) -> 88 wins the audience comparison -> slots 5-7 = 88, 198 goes to slot 9.
# (With the half-day range of fix "ai-odd-range" the odd-length rule keeps the 3-hour film 88
# out and 129 wins instead; classic, the original's stale range 1..0 never rejects it.)

# expect fixed   40000 word 39D4:44D5 == 88
# expect fixed   40000 word 39D4:44DD == 198
